Record Class LimitKey

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
grafiosch.dto.LimitKey
Record Components:
limitType - which mechanism the key configures, never null
entityName - JPA entity simple name or a registered pseudo name such as HistoryquoteRead
relationEntityName - element entity of a nested-collection limit, null for a flat cap
countScope - per parent or across all parents, null for a flat cap
ownerScope - how existing rows are counted, null for the daily types
public record LimitKey(LimitType limitType, String entityName, String relationEntityName, CountScope countScope, OwnerScope ownerScope) extends Record
Identifies one configurable limit. It is the tuple stored in the five key columns of entity_limit and the unit the resolver and the limit key registry work with.

The key space has two halves. LimitType.MAX keys are registered explicitly, because a counter, a parent relation, two scopes and a message key cannot be derived from an entity name. LimitType.DAY_CUD and LimitType.DAY_READ keys are derived from the JPA metamodel plus the registered pseudo entity names, because their counter is always user_entity_change_count and they have neither relation nor scopes.

    • keyId

      public String keyId()
      Stable wire identifier: the five parts joined with "|", an empty segment for every null part. This is what the admin edit form posts back, so it must stay parseable by parse(String).
      Returns:
      for example MAX|Watchlist|Securitycurrency|SINGLE|TENANT or DAY_CUD|Assetclass|||

    • parse

      public static LimitKey parse(String keyId)
      Reverses keyId(). The caller must still check the result against the registry or the derived set — a syntactically valid key id is not necessarily a key that exists.
      Parameters:
      keyId - the five parts joined with "|"
      Returns:
      the parsed key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the shape or one of the enum constants is unknown
